title: Hiragana Sound Change Check
concept: Dakuten, handakuten, small kana, and long vowels

questions.prompt: What happens when dakuten is added to か?
questions.explanation: Dakuten voices the k-row: k becomes g, so か ka becomes が ga.

questions.prompt: What sound does the small circle add to the h-row?

options.label: A p sound, as in ぱ pa
A b sound, as in ば ba
A g sound, as in が ga

questions.explanation: Handakuten is the small circle that changes h-row kana to p-row sounds.

questions.prompt: Which spelling reads kitte, stamp, with a held consonant?
questions.explanation: Small っ holds the following t sound; it is not pronounced as a full tsu.

questions.prompt: Why does きょう begin with kyo rather than ki-yo?

options.label: ょ is small and combines with き.
き is followed by small っ.

questions.explanation: Small ょ contracts with the preceding i-row kana, so きょ is one contracted sound kyo.

questions.prompt: Which word has the long a sound in obaasan, grandmother?
questions.explanation: The extra あ extends the a sound. おばさん without it means aunt.

questions.prompt: Put the beginner decoding checks in a useful order.

items.label: Apply small っ to the next consonant

questions.explanation: Reading the visible marks and sizes before guessing the whole word prevents common beginner errors.
